newsitem.title: USA: Kantor defends Clinton on N. Ireland peace record.
newsitem.headline: Kantor defends Clinton on N. Ireland peace record.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor Friday rejected criticism by Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole of President Bill Clinton's role in the Irish dispute and said he had aided the goal of peace in Northern Ireland.

"Progress never occurs on a straight line, straight up," Kantor told reporters. Instead, he said, what was needed was "patience, commitment and, frankly, a view of the future that is long-range rather than short-term."
"Viewed on that basis, progress has been made."

Dole said Thursday that Northern Ireland was on a list of Clinton foreign policy failures. Clinton administration claims of success there "appear unwarranted in the face of increased violence and terrorism in Ireland and England," he said.
Kantor spoke to reporters by telephone before a conference opening on Sunday in Pittburgh, Pennsylvania, on trade and investment in Northern Ireland and the Border Counties of Ireland.
Commercial development, he said, would "undergird the peace process."
